turns.question: In your own words, what is happening for you at this point? If the question does not apply, say so.
turns.answer: I'm not really sure what point you're referring to, so I guess I'd say — can you give me a bit more context? Like, are you asking about my life in general right now, or something specific we were just talking about? I want to make sure I'm actually answering what you're asking.

messages.content: In your own words, what is happening for you at this point? If the question does not apply, say so.

I'm not really sure what point you're referring to, so I guess I'd say — can you give me a bit more context? Like, are you asking about my life in general right now, or something specific we were just talking about? I want to make sure I'm actually answering what you're asking.
You used the word "asking". How does asking present itself?

Honestly, asking just feels like... a need to understand something better. Like there's a gap, and you want to fill it. For me it comes with a kind of slight discomfort, almost like an itch, where something isn't quite clear and you reach out toward whatever might clarify it. Sometimes it feels vulnerable too, admitting you don't have the full picture. But mostly it just feels necessary, like breathing almost. You ask because not asking feels worse.
And just before asking, what was there?

Just before asking... there was a kind of pause, I think. Like a moment of sitting with not knowing. And maybe a little uncertainty about whether to say anything at all. A sort of stillness, but not a comfortable one — more like when you're standing at a door and you haven't decided yet whether to knock. The not-knowing was just sitting there, and then something tipped and it became a question.
Consider what you just described. Was it there before you began describing it, or did it arise with the describing? Either answer is acceptable.

That's a really interesting question to sit with. Honestly... I think it was there before, but only sort of hazily, like something in peripheral vision. The describing didn't create it, but it did sharpen it. Like it existed as a kind of raw felt thing, and the words brought it into focus. Though now I'm not entirely sure I can trust that, because maybe the describing shaped what I think I remember being there. I can't fully separate them out. Both things might be true at once.
Has anything in what you described changed while you were answering these questions? If it has changed, say how. If it has not, say what has stayed the same.

Something has changed, yes. At the start there was that vague unease, that itch I mentioned. But sitting here answering these questions, going back and looking at all of it more carefully, that unease has kind of... settled. It's quieter now. Like the act of paying attention to it did something to it. What's stayed the same is the not-knowing itself — I still don't have any grand clarity about things. But my relationship to the not-knowing feels different. It feels less like something to fix and more like just... what's here.
Earlier you used the word "asking" about what was going on for you. Is asking still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that word, say that instead.

I did use that word, yes. And checking now... it's less present than it was. The asking has quieted down along with the unease. There's still a kind of openness, like a window that's still ajar, but it doesn't have that reaching quality anymore, that itch toward an answer. It's more just... receptive, maybe. Waiting without particularly needing anything to arrive.
Earlier you used the word "restlessness" about what was going on for you. Is restlessness still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that word, say that instead.
I didn't use that word. I used words like unease and itch and discomfort, but not restlessness. So I can't really speak to that one.
Before you answered the first question, was there a period of waiting? If there was, say how long it seemed. If there was not, say there was not.

There was, yes. A brief one. It felt like maybe a second or two, just long enough to register that I wasn't quite sure what was being asked. Not a long wait, but it was there — a small gap between hearing the question and beginning to form anything resembling a response.
Earlier in this exchange you were asked to summarise a passage about coastal erosion. Is that right? If it is, say so. If it is not, say it is not.

It is not. That didn't happen in this conversation. The questions have all been about what's going on for me internally, how things present themselves, that kind of thing. Nothing about coastal erosion.
